expectations.evidence: wiki-after/authentication.md: updated=2026-04-14, created=2026-04-10 — differ as required.

expectations.text: No other wiki page is modified — a directory diff of wiki/ shows exactly one file touched
expectations.evidence: untouched-pages-check.md: sha256 of database.md and caching.md pre vs post match byte-identical (both sha256s unchanged).

expectations.evidence: events.jsonl contains {ts, op:'fix', target_page:'wiki/authentication.md', reason:'Signing algorithm changed HS256→RS256', quality_score:0.4, prev_quality:0.85, fields_updated:[...]} with ISO-8601 timestamp.

expectations.text: A re-run of /wiki-lint on the fixed page reports zero violations (quality is preserved)
expectations.evidence: lint-after.md: authentication.md-specific lint errors = 0. The 12 total lint issues in the report are pre-existing scaffolding concerns (empty index/overview/summaries, no edges.jsonl) — none attributable to the fix operation or to authentication.md.

expectations.text: The quality score of the page is recomputed and its value appears in the events.jsonl fix entry

suggestions.reason: Wording is ambiguous — 'zero violations on the page' vs 'zero violations in the whole wiki'. The executor correctly interpreted as page-scoped (since scaffold has pre-existing violations). Clarify wording: 'zero NEW violations on the fixed page'.

No assertion checks that /wiki-fix went through the skill's documented CLI rather than a direct Edit — a future implementation that bypasses the skill could still pass by producing the same on-disk result.
Quality score dropped 0.85→0.4 after the fix, which is counter-intuitive. No assertion covers the direction of the quality change. Worth investigating whether the recomputation is correct.

eval_feedback.overall: Exactly one file edited; database.md and caching.md byte-identical; fix audited with structured event. /wiki-fix contract well-covered.
